**Yes, it can be approved, but not by Sarah Chen herself. Michael Torres, the VP of Sales, has to approve it.**

**Why:** The Northstar Pricing Policy 2026 applies from 2026-01-01 to 2026-12-31, so it covers 2026-09-23. It sets three approval levels:
- Discounts up to and including 10%: the Enterprise Account Executive can approve them.
- Discounts above 10% and up to 20%: the VP of Sales must approve them.
- Discounts above 20%: the Chief Revenue Officer (David Morgan) must approve them.

Sarah Chen is an Enterprise Account Executive, so her limit is 10%. A 15% discount falls in the VP of Sales band. The VP of Sales is Michael Torres, and she has reported to him since 2026-09-01. Two roles are named in the policy: "Account Executive" and "Chief Revenue Officer". Sarah's title uses the policy's own wording. If you mean something different by "Acme" or "sales director", let me know.

**Things I couldn't confirm:**
- **DR-9001 has no details on record.** I couldn't confirm from the records that it's for 15% or which Acme customer it covers. There are two: ACME Manufacturing and Acme Industrial Supply Co. What the records do show is a discount request on the Acme NS-500 dated 2026-09-23. So the 15% figure comes from your question.
- **Sarah's name is linked to an older request.** The records also say an Acme NS-500 request was made by Sarah Chen on 2025-09-16. The 2026-09-23 request doesn't say who made it. Two other people have also asked for NS-500 discounts this year: Zachary Brown in March and Kelly Floyd in July. You may want to check that DR-9001 is really Sarah's.
- **There's nothing on absences or delegation.** I found no record of Michael Torres being away on 2026-09-23 or handing his approval authority to someone else.
